_meta.purpose: Audit-grade nameplate-capacity citations for facility-engineering edges. Each entry pins the edge weight to a primary-source disclosure (operator IR materials, EIA country briefs, S&P Platts, etc.) rather than a fitted statistical relationship.
_meta.weight_convention: weight encodes fraction of source-facility throughput that is committed to the target. weight=1.0 means the source is dedicated to the target; weight<1.0 means the throughput is split across multiple downstream nodes. Where a single dedicated downstream link exists, weight=1.0 is appropriate even though the graph 'weight' field also encodes propagation strength under shock.
_meta.lag_convention: lag is in days. For pipeline/throughput edges, propagation is sub-daily under normal operation; we use lag=1 as the discrete-time minimum. For batch/marine/inventoried flows, lag reflects approximate transit + buffering.
_meta.confidence_convention: confidence reflects how recent and how directly attributable the underlying disclosure is. >=0.9 = primary operator disclosure within last 24 months; 0.7-0.85 = secondary aggregator (EIA, Platts) within last 5 years; <0.7 = older or indirect attribution.
_meta.scope: This file is intentionally seeded with high-leverage keystone edges only. The remaining ~50 capacity_citation edges retain their expert-prior weights pending follow-up sourcing. Schema is stable; new entries can be appended without touching code.

primary_source.title: East-West Crude Oil Pipeline (Petroline)
key_facts: Pipeline capacity ~5 mb/d after the 2019 expansion (Aramco IR materials)
Routes Eastern Province crude to Yanbu on the Red Sea coast for export and west-coast refining
Single dedicated linear asset; no parallel route at this scale

secondary_source.title: Country Analysis Brief: Saudi Arabia
secondary_source.url_search_hint: EIA Saudi Arabia country analysis brief

citations.weight_rationale: Single-route-to-target with no near-term substitute -> weight=1.0. Disruption propagates immediately (next-day pricing) under shock.

primary_source.title: Saudi Arabia crude oil production outage affects global crude oil and gasoline prices
key_facts: Abqaiq processes ~7 mb/d, the world's largest crude stabilization facility
Abqaiq output feeds the East-West Pipeline among other downstream routes
September 2019 attack removed 5.7 mb/d of Saudi crude from global supply for ~3 weeks

citations.weight_rationale: Abqaiq is upstream of nearly all Saudi crude flows; the East-West Pipeline is one of multiple committed downstreams. Weight=1.0 reflects the fact that any Abqaiq disruption flows directly into pipeline volumes; the *fractional* split across pipeline vs Ras Tanura terminal vs domestic refining is captured by the relative weights on the multiple outgoing edges from Abqaiq.

primary_source.title: Saudi Arabia crude oil production outage affects global crude oil and gasoline prices
key_facts: Ras Tanura is Saudi Arabia's main crude export terminal (~6 mb/d throughput)
Receives the majority of Abqaiq-stabilized crude bound for Asian export markets
Throughput share vs East-West Pipeline approximately 75-85% in normal operation

citations.weight_rationale: Majority but not all of Abqaiq output flows east to Ras Tanura under normal conditions; the rest splits across the East-West Pipeline (Yanbu) and domestic refineries. 0.85 reflects the throughput share.

primary_source.title: Hawiyah Gas Plant capacity disclosures
key_facts: Hawiyah is one of the major non-associated gas processing plants feeding the Master Gas System
Roughly 2.5 bcf/d processing capacity post-expansion
Output dedicated to MGS for distribution to power generation, petrochemical, and water desalination customers

citations.weight_rationale: Hawiyah's processed gas is essentially fully committed to MGS distribution; small reservation for site fuel use and local feedstock keeps weight just under 1.0.

primary_source.title: QAFCO trains 1-4 production capacities
key_facts: QAFCO 1-4 are the older urea trains at Mesaieed Industrial City
Combined train 1-4 urea nameplate ~3.1 MTPA out of ~5.6 MTPA total complex
Trains 5 and 6 add the remaining ~2.5 MTPA on the same site

citations.weight_rationale: Trains 1-4 contribute roughly 55% of the complex's urea throughput; trains 5-6 contribute the remaining 45%. Both feed the same product stream.

primary_source.title: QAFCO trains 5-6 production capacities
key_facts: QAFCO 5 and 6 are the newer urea trains commissioned 2011-2012
Combined nameplate ~2.5 MTPA
Trains 5 and 6 incorporate carbon-capture for downstream blue-ammonia integration

citations.weight_rationale: Trains 5-6 contribute roughly 45% of the complex's urea throughput; complement to trains 1-4 (55%).

primary_source.title: Ras Al Khair phosphoric acid -> DAP integration
key_facts: Phosphoric acid is the primary feedstock for DAP (di-ammonium phosphate) production
Ras Al Khair phosphoric acid units are integrated on-site with the DAP plant; no merchant offtake of phosphoric acid at scale
Stoichiometry: ~1.5 t H3PO4 per t DAP at typical operating concentrations

citations.weight_rationale: Phosphoric acid units are essentially dedicated to the on-site DAP plant; small reservation for MAP/NPK side-streams keeps weight just under 1.0.
